text:
Evan P.: hey team, just got an escalation from a high-traffic customer — they're seeing p95/p99 spikes on generate calls after last night's deploy. customer reports latency regressions only when using function-calling / tool router + structured JSON outputs.

Priya K.: ugh. do we have a ticket id or example request?

Evan P.: ticket #INC-4729. repro payload attached in the ticket but quick example: function-calling with 4 tools + strict JSON schema in the response. p95 up from ~120ms -> ~340ms, p99 from ~480ms -> ~1.2s.

Carlos M.: I pulled traces for that customer and correlated traces to the tool-router service. here's the span breakdown from jaeger for one slow request:
```
tool-router.request  -  total 1240ms
  - route.select    70ms
  - validate-input  15ms
  - call-tool-1     320ms
  - call-tool-2     310ms
  - validate-json-schema (post-tool)  220ms
  - assemble-response  150ms
  - response-send    55ms
```
validate-json-schema is the unusual one — we've never seen it dominate like this. median for that span jumped to ~180-240ms in the last 3 hours for this tenant.

Sasha L.: any code changes that touched router/validation in the deploy?

deploy-bot: new deploy completed by @deploy-pipeline at 2024-11-10T03:12:40Z (sha: a1b2c3).

Priya K.: yes, yesterday's deploy added synchronous JSON schema validation on the critical path to catch malformed structured outputs earlier. intention was to fail-fast and surface schema errors to customers. looks like it made validation CPU-heavy for big schemas + nested arrays.

Evan P.: customer wants an immediate mitigation; they're on dedicated capacity but SLA impact. recommended steps?

Sasha L.: quick mitigations: 1) toggle per-tenant feature-flag to disable strict validation on the router (fast). 2) roll validation off the critical path -> async validation and background telemetry. 3) increase router replicas temporarily to absorb overhead. 4) short canary rollback of the deploy.

Carlos M.: to reproduce locally I used this curl: 
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-3","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"call tools"}],"function_call":{"name":"auto"},"tools":[{"name":"tool1","schema":{...}},{"name":"tool2","schema":{...}}],"max_tokens":512}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
```
If you add a header to bypass validation (we have an internal header for tests) it drops latency back down: add `x-internal-skip-json-validate: 1` and p95/p99 return to baseline.

infra-bot: flagged: increased 5xx errors and latency for service=tool-router in us-west-2; alert: SR-92.

Priya K.: sounds like we should flip the feature flag for the affected customer and restore perf immediately while we ship a proper fix. who can flip and own customer comms?

Carlos M.: I can flip flag and run a small smoke test against the customer's workload. will also capture post-flag p95/p99.

Sasha L.: I'll prepare a small code patch to move heavy JSON validation into an async worker queue + add lightweight shape-check on the hot path. patch target: router/validation v1.1.1 -> v1.1.2. Carlos, after you flip flag can you run `kubectl rollout restart deploy/tool-router -n prod-us-west-2` for a soft refresh if we need extra capacity?

Evan P.: also want to communicate to the customer: immediate mitigation (disabling strict validation) and ETA for a fix (we'll commit to async validation + opt-in strict checks). I'll draft a message once you confirm flag flip and smoke results.

Carlos M.: flipped flag for tenant id=acct-9987 at 2024-11-10T04:05Z. smoke run shows p95 ~130ms, p99 ~460ms for the sample workload. pushing logs to ticket now.

Priya K.: awesome. next: code fix timeline?

Sasha L.: I can get a PR by EOD with unit tests, integration tests, and a migration plan. expect 24-36h for full rollout (canary -> prod). immediate release will have: - lightweight structural assertions on hot path (cheap) - enqueue full JSON schema validation off-path - metrics/alerts to flag schema failures so we don't lose telemetry.

Evan P.: perfect. I'll update the customer: temporary toggle applied, perf restored, full fix in progress, ETA ~36h. include suggestion to avoid super-large nested schemas for now.

Priya K.: follow-up: we should also add schema validation timing to our console per-route dashboard (p95 of validation span) so we can catch this earlier. filing infra ticket.

Sasha L.: filed INFRA-2145 for validation-timing dashboard and an alert where validate-json-schema p95 > 150ms.

Evan P.: thanks everyone. action items: Carlos flip + smoke (done), Sasha patch + PR, Priya coordinate customer comms, infra ticket filed. I'll close the loop in the ticket once PR merges. :thumbsup:

Carlos M.: adding final note — long-term we should consider caching compiled validators per-schema-id (reuse Ajv compiled func) and batch validating tool outputs where possible to reduce repeated compile cost. that should drop median validation by ~70%.

Sasha L.: agreed. add to backlog for Optimize team as well.

infra-bot: incident SR-92 acknowledged, status: mitigated (validation toggle applied).
